scope: Rapid targeted prior-art check for stage2 stable variable selection and few-label calibration; not a systematic or exhaustive novelty review

references.title: Key wavelengths screening using competitive adaptive reweighted sampling method for multivariate calibration
references.verified_scope: PubMed bibliographic record and full abstract; publisher indexed abstract
references.relevant_existing_idea: PLS coefficient importance, Monte Carlo sampling, exponential reduction and adaptive reweighting; CV subset choice.
references.implication_for_stage2: Existing CARS and CARS-style roots require attribution. Resampling CARS supports is an engineering extension until a clearly differentiated method and external evidence are established.
references.not_claimed: Exact reproduction of archived MATLAB behavior by the independent Python selector.

references.title: A variable selection method based on uninformative variable elimination for multivariate calibration of near-infrared spectra
references.verified_scope: Indexed publisher title/abstract and bibliographic metadata; direct full publisher open returned403; full text not reviewed
references.relevant_existing_idea: Random calibration subsets and stability of PLS coefficients for modified UVE.
references.implication_for_stage2: MC-UVE is an established coefficient-stability method; adding another resampling layer needs a matched-count baseline and a reason beyond the name.
references.not_claimed: Full source-level correspondence to every MC-UVE variant.

references.title: An ensemble of Monte Carlo uninformative variable elimination for wavelength selection
references.verified_scope: PubMed indexed bibliographic record and abstract; publisher indexed abstract
references.relevant_existing_idea: An ensemble combines MC-UVE and a vote rule for wavelength selection.
references.implication_for_stage2: This is especially close prior art for repeated MC-UVE plus selection-frequency voting. The proposed wrapper must not be described as a new voting/stability principle.
references.not_claimed: The current wrapper reproduces the original ensemble algorithm or its tuning details.

references.title: Stability Selection
references.journal: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 72(4):417–473
references.verified_scope: Publisher bibliographic metadata and author preprint abstract
references.relevant_existing_idea: Subsampling combined with selection algorithms; finite-sample error-control results under specified assumptions/settings.
references.implication_for_stage2: A generic frequency-of-selection score or top-k rule is not automatically a p-value, FDR bound or theorem-backed stability-selection procedure.
references.not_claimed: Theoretical false-discovery control for the stage2 selector.

references.title: Algorithm of Stability-Analysis-Based Feature Selection for NIR Calibration Transfer
references.verified_scope: Open full text, especially §§2.1–2.2 and data-availability statement
references.relevant_existing_idea: Master/slave PLS coefficient stability is estimated through Monte Carlo sampling; a GA selects a threshold using validation performance; selected variables are combined with established transfer methods.
references.implication_for_stage2: Stable variable selection plus transfer is already a research direction. Our single-source resample-frequency wrapper differs from SAFS but does not by itself establish novelty. A proper future comparison should state whether target paired standards are available.
references.data_availability: Corn is a public referenced dataset; authors state their presented data are available on request and not all publicly available. Larch data must not be counted as downloaded.
references.not_claimed: The current wrapper implements SAFS or has its reported transfer performance.

references.title: A Review of Calibration Transfer Practices and Instrument Differences in Spectroscopy
references.verified_scope: PubMed bibliographic record/abstract and indexed publisher text
references.relevant_existing_idea: Robust calibration, bias/slope adjustment and spectral standardization are established approaches; instrument uncertainty and repeatability matter.
references.implication_for_stage2: Few-shot affine correction should be a clear established baseline. Matching instruments, reference chemistry and specimen presentation must be reported.
references.not_claimed: Successful instrument transfer proves across-year or across-herb generalization.

references.title: Standardisation and Calibration Transfer for near Infrared Instruments: A Review
references.verified_scope: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata; restricted full text not claimed read
references.relevant_existing_idea: Pooling instruments for robustness, modest labeled transfer sets for slope/bias adjustment, and paired measured spectra for spectral standardization.
references.implication_for_stage2: Bias-only/affine correction is not a novel calibration concept; DS/PDS needs paired standards from support, not query.
references.not_claimed: Regularized affine engineering is a new discovery merely because the support set is small.

references.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
references.verified_scope: Publisher indexed metadata/abstract; direct open403; no full-text review claimed
references.implication_for_stage2: Penalizing departure from an identity coefficient/score mapping is an engineering use of ridge/prior anchoring. This reference supports the regularization family, not an assertion that our exact calibrator appeared in this paper.
references.not_claimed: Specific near-infrared identity-anchored calibration algorithm is attributed to this paper.

module_characterization.StableVariableSelector: Independent engineering wrapper around established CARS-style/MC-UVE selectors, repeated training-unit subsampling and fixed-count frequency ranking. Close voting ensemble prior art exists.
module_characterization.ShrinkageAffineCalibrator: Regularized slope/bias correction toward identity, evaluated only using labeled target support. Established affine/regularization ideas; performance to be tested.
module_characterization.AnchorScoreCalibrator: Regularized identity-anchored mapping of source class scores; explicit source class vocabulary. An engineering candidate, not asserted new or probability-calibrated.

protocol_decisions.decision: Keep original five outer folds for ablation but label results reanalysis of an already-inspected benchmark. No new untouched confirmation set is created by re-running it.
protocol_decisions.reason: Earlier test results were used to select the research direction.

protocol_decisions.decision: For each repetition create a fixed query set and a separate support candidate pool; use nested support prefixes for n=1,3,5,10,... and the same query/IDs for all methods.
protocol_decisions.reason: Changing query composition with shot count confounds learning curves.

protocol_decisions.decision: Fix regularization/feature count/iterations before target query evaluation, or select only on source-domain nested validation/pseudo-domain episodes.
protocol_decisions.reason: Selecting by final target labels leaks test information.

protocol_decisions.decision: Keep physical specimen groups out of source/support/query intersections. Recovered metadata row keys are an auditable proxy, not proof of physical or batch identity.
protocol_decisions.reason: The same specimen measured on different instruments cannot be called unseen-plant generalization.

protocol_decisions.decision: Compare stable and nonstable selectors at matched retained feature counts, with identical downstream grid, while reporting extra resampling/fits/runtime separately.
protocol_decisions.reason: Dimension and compute-budget changes otherwise confound a stability effect.
